w: This Cathedral City mausoleum, just outside Palm Springs, operated for decades as the Palm Springs Mortuary and Mausoleum before Forest Lawn Memorial-Parks and Mortuaries renamed it in 2005, folding it into the same operator behind the famed Los Angeles Forest Lawn cemeteries.
s: Renamed in 2005 from Palm Springs Mortuary and Mausoleum
_facts: Formerly named Palm Springs Mortuary and Mausoleum
Renamed Forest Lawn Memorial Park in 2005
Operated by Forest Lawn Memorial-Parks and Mortuaries

w: John Lautner built this 1968 hilltop house on Southridge Drive for designer Arthur Elrod, excavating the soil but leaving granite boulders in place, running through the walls and windows. A circular concrete canopy shelters the living room, opening onto a pool with a view of Palm Springs and San Jacinto Peak.
s: Lautner's rock-through-the-walls house on Southridge Drive
_facts: Designed by John Lautner, built 1968 for Arthur Elrod
2175 Southridge Drive, on the edge of a hill
Native rocks left in place, running through walls and windows
Large circular concrete canopy over the living room, opening to a pool and view of San Jacinto Peak

w: Founded in 1938 as the Palm Springs Desert Museum, the institution has focused on design and contemporary art since 2004. Its Palm Springs campus pairs the art museum with an Architecture and Design Center, while a satellite Faye Sarkowsky Sculpture Garden sits in Palm Desert.
